subject: Acme production: urgent degradation notice — 5xx/429 spike after model update

To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Karthik,

We just started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx/429 errors and request timeouts across our production traffic for the Redwood-hosted endpoint (us-west-2). This started ~08:50 PDT after the model rollout you mentioned on the call (v4q-2026.09.28). Affected clients are timing out inside our app and we're seeing retry storms from client-side backoff that amplify the problem.

Sample error: 429 Too Many Requests returned on nearly all short (<2s) requests. Attached is a short log snippet and one of our request traces. Can you confirm whether you rolled a quantized kernel or changed a config today? We need an ETA on a rollback or mitigation.

Attachments: error_snapshot.json (log snippet)

Subject: Fwd: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Folks — Jordan flagged a customer-facing outage in Acme production immediately after today's canary rollout (v4q-2026.09.28). Summary: elevated 5xx/429, client retry amplification, visible latency regressions.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra/SRE confirm whether the rollout included a quantization profile change or a new fused kernel?
- If so, can we rollback the canary and stop the rollout to additional capacity?
- Marissa: please coordinate comms with Acme (apology + immediate mitigation plan).
- Rishi/Evelyn: can you join a 15-min triage call now? I'll set up a bridge.

I attached a short impact summary I'm drafting for Acme.

Attachments: acme_impact_summary.pdf

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Karthik / team — quick triage notes from infra side (SRE + serving runtime):
1) Canary rollout introduced a changed quantization profile (int8 aggressive pack) and a kernel selector tweak for short-sequence low-latency paths.
2) On canary hosts we see increased KV cache misses and a spike in lock contention inside the new fused-kernel path starting 08:48 PDT. That leads to higher tail latency and 429s when autoscaling queues back up.
3) Immediate mitigation: initiated canary rollback for the us-west-2 canary pool at 09:30 PDT — rollback is in progress.
4) Longer-term: we need to revert the quantization profile for this workload and run microbenchmarks against Acme's typical seq-len distribution.

I'm pushing a temporary routing rule to divert Acme traffic to the older model variant (v4q-stable) while rollback completes. I'll share rollback commands.

Attachments: rollback_commands.sh

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Jordan — we are very sorry for the disruption. We started an immediate rollback of the canary at 09:30 PDT and have applied a hotfix routing override to send Acme traffic to the prior stable model variant. You should see errors drop within the next 10–15 minutes; we're monitoring.

Next steps we propose (short):
- Complete canary rollback and verify health across us-west-2 (timeline: 30–45 minutes).
- Run post-rollback validation with your SRE test harness and share results.
- Root cause follow-up: we'll run a focused investigation into quantization / kernel interaction and send a detailed postmortem within 48 hours.

Would you like us to open a scheduled maintenance window to re-run a safer rollout with restricted concurrency?

Again, apologies — we will share continuous updates on this thread and via the incident status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-09-28-acme-5xx

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Customer impact: transient user-facing errors (some request retries), no data loss reported. Potential revenue impact if sustained (enterprise SLA).

Asks for leadership:
- Approve a 48-hour high-priority postmortem with cross-team allocation (Serving, Infra, Product, QA).
- Consider a temporary freeze on quantization-profile changes for enterprise customers until we complete regression tests.

I'll prepare the PM notes and postmortem draft; flagging to Naomi Feldman and the GTM leadership for awareness.
